title: Carve a Ski Tiki
lines: A plain log. A big grin. And one very cool ski tiki.
Here's the process, from sketch to lodge legend.

title: Sketch the personality
note: Secure the log. Think big shapes.
lines: Start with a stable, securely clamped log.
Sketch oversized goggles, a broad grin, and an owl on top.

title: Find the silhouette
lines: Suit up with proper chainsaw protection.
Rough out the silhouette in stages, leaving extra wood around the details.

title: Make that grin
lines: Define the nose, mouth, and teeth.
Work gradually: deep shadows make that grin read from across the room.

title: Give it character
note: An owl up top. Texture below.
lines: Shape the owl and add feather lines.
Refine the body pattern, checking the whole carving as you go.

title: Bring out the grain
note: Before coatings • keep fire protection nearby
lines: Before any paint or finish, a light scorch brings out texture.
Work clear of combustibles, with fire protection nearby.

title: Make the details pop
note: Let it cool. Brush off loose char.
lines: Let the wood cool, then brush away loose char.
Darken the recesses and wipe back the raised surfaces.

title: Add ski-day color
lines: Then give those goggles a fiery red-to-gold fade.
Now it's looking ready for the slopes.

title: Lodge legend.
note: For outdoor display: choose a compatible exterior finish.
lines: Choose a protective finish suited to where it'll live.
One log. One owl. Maximum après-ski attitude.
